summary: CLI/tooling review completed. Clean install, ESLint, overlay syntax checks, controller contracts, voice-crypto contracts, YAML parsing, referenced-file checks, and expected Linux WPF build artifact all passed. Syntax mutations were caught by both ESLint and the verifier. One contract-test weakness was reproduced: changing only the production ROOM ENCRYPTION UNAVAILABLE occurrence does not fail because the same token remains in a second branch.

minor.issue: Contract check uses source-wide String.includes. voice.js contains ROOM ENCRYPTION UNAVAILABLE twice; changing one production error branch leaves the duplicate token and the verifier exits 0, so a branch-specific regression is not caught.

action_items: Strengthen the sealed-signaling contract to verify each required failure branch or the expected occurrence count/context, rather than accepting one source-wide token occurrence.
critical_code_review_comments: Token-presence contracts are useful smoke tests but can false-pass when a duplicated literal survives elsewhere; bind this security-sensitive assertion to the capability-guard branch and deriveSignalKey failure branch (or assert both occurrences and surrounding structure).
context_for_next_testing_agent: No services/browser are involved. Final tree checks are green. Build emits expected Linux MSB3030 after producing /app/BurntHud/bin/Release/net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0/Isley.dll. Regression mutations were restored byte-for-byte to the pre-test working copy.
rca_of_the_issue: verify-overlay-scripts.cjs checks voice.includes("'ROOM ENCRYPTION UNAVAILABLE'"). The literal occurs at both the missing-crypto capability guard and deriveSignalKey catch. A one-occurrence production mutation leaves the other occurrence, satisfying includes and producing a false pass. Reproduction: replace only the first occurrence, observe token count 2 to 1, then run node scripts/verify-overlay-scripts.cjs; it exits 0. Replacing both occurrences correctly exits non-zero and names the missing contract.
